question: Should already-published version changelogs be mutable, and if so what authorization, audit trail, and consumer-visible revision semantics must the correction workflow enforce?
rationale: The request adds a new capability over published release records; code review cannot safely choose whether releases are immutable, append-only with corrections, or directly editable.

options.title: Append audited corrections
options.body: Permit authorized publishers to add a revision that preserves the originally published changelog and exposes correction metadata to consumers.

options.title: Keep releases immutable
options.body: Reject post-publication edits and provide a documented superseding-release or correction-note workflow instead.

options.title: Allow direct replacement
options.body: Permit in-place edits only after maintainers define strong authorization, audit retention, and downstream-cache behavior.

recommendation.title: Append audited corrections
recommendation.body: Permit authorized publishers to add a revision that preserves the originally published changelog and exposes correction metadata to consumers.

likelyOwner.reason: No concrete owner can be established from the available current-main history evidence.
